summary: 1942 U.S. Forest Service fire tower on the Oconee National Forest in Greene County, Georgia; fenced behind a locked gate at the last report (October 2016).

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Oconee Ranger District cooperator)

staffing.status: Register staffing field reads Yes; the 2016 steward report names no lookout

access.note: Fenced, with a gate locked with Rayle EMC padlocks at the October 2016 steward visit. The Register gives no public-access terms and records no posted sign.

visit.trail_note: Site fenced behind a locked gate; the 2016 steward could only see the tower from outside the fence.

events.note: Built by the U.S. Forest Service per the Register

Steward visit October 9, 2016, from outside the fence: glass in the cab appears intact, metal sides and roof rusty, four antennas of unknown owners, small building inside the fence with power and antenna lines

evidence.supports: built 1942 by the U.S. Forest Service
evidence.quote: Built by the U.S. Forest Service 1942

evidence.supports: on the Oconee National Forest in central Georgia
evidence.quote: It is located on the Oconee National Forest in central Georgia.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
site fenced; gate locked with Rayle EMC padlocks
evidence.quote: This tower is fenced off with a gate locked with Rayle EMC padlocks.

evidence.supports: steward had no access inside the fence
evidence.quote: I do not have access to the inside of the fence.

evidence.supports: steward observed from outside the locked gate
evidence.quote: My notation of wood and glass conditions are based on what I can see from outside the locked gate.

evidence.supports: glass in the cab appears intact through binoculars
evidence.quote: Looking at the tower through binoculars, the glass in the hut on top appears to be intact.
The metal sides and roof appear rusty.
There are four antennas attached to the tower, owners unknown (by me).

evidence.supports: small building inside the fence with power and antenna lines
evidence.quote: There is a small building inside the fence at the base of the tower with an electrical line running to it and antenna lines off the tower going to the building.
I have volunteered to be the tower steward for the Oakland Fire Tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The visit form marks the tower in good condition, while the steward's comments note rusty metal and that the assessment was made from outside the locked fence. The story reports both and does not rate the tower beyond the 2016 report.
The Register's staffing field reads Yes, but the 2016 steward report describes a fenced, locked site and names no lookout. The story reports the field and the gap without resolving it.

notes_for_editor: One source only: the NHLR page with its 2016 steward report. Two web searches found no staffing history, fire history or post-2016 report. Brief's access 'unknown' updated to restricted from the locked gate. Height converted from 80 ft to 24.4 m. Brief's registry and coordinates match the NHLR page.
